# Independent audit: facet zonoids and prescribed inside allocations

Audit date: 2026-09-20. Auditor: research-agent.

**Result: PASS, with the exact necessary-condition scope stated in the
source.** This is an independent audit of
`candidate 9c6d3cb586898f7e`
(A3), including the uses it makes of the allocation/separation arguments
in `candidate a68c14b477a24d06` and
`candidate beffb23a92dd631a`. No source file was
changed.

The hypotheses are finitely many positive, full d-dimensional compact
convex fibers, d>=1. The local cap assertion concerns a depth-attaining
nonvertical cap through a point interior to its own fiber. The stress
assertion additionally uses a true local minimum and one of the critical
cover systems allowed in the two stress sources. None of these results
proves a numerical OC bound. In particular the arbitrary finite-base
gamma_d/h(P) target is false; the corrected OC reduction must retain
lattice completeness and its parity budget.

## 1. Independent derivation of the directional cap derivative

Write the cap as a.p+v.x>=b, with |v|=1, and fix a base p. Put
c=b-a.p. In the continuous coordinates write x=z+s v, where z is in
v-perpendicular. The projection D of the fiber onto v-perpendicular is
a compact convex set. Almost every z in D has a nondegenerate fiber
interval [l(z),u(z)]. The exceptional projected boundary has
(d-1)-dimensional measure zero. For d=1 this is the same assertion over
the singleton zero-dimensional projection, and the interval is
nondegenerate by the positive-fiber hypothesis.

Perturb the full normal by t e, and the threshold by t e.y. At the
old cap plane let

    ell(p,z+c v)=e.((p,z+c v)-y).

For small t the new cut in this line is s>=c+delta_t(z), where exactly

    delta_t(z)=-t ell(p,z+c v)/(1+t e_x.v).

The denominator stays positive. On the bounded projection,
delta_t/t converges uniformly to -ell, and |delta_t|<=C|t|. The cap
length on the interval is

    [u(z)-max(l(z),c+delta_t(z))]_+.

Its right derivative at zero is ell if l<c<u, min(0,ell) if c=l<u,
max(0,ell) if l<c=u, and zero when c is strictly outside the interval.
All difference quotients are bounded by one common constant, so
Fubini and dominated convergence justify integrating this exact formula.

If the plane cuts the fiber interior, its section is a full
(d-1)-dimensional convex body in that plane. Points of this section
which are on the fiber boundary have section measure zero: a relative
interior section point lies in the fiber interior when the cutting
plane meets that interior. Thus the first case contributes precisely
the proper-section integral. If the plane supports the fiber, its
positive-area section is exactly the indicated inside or outside
facet; the second or third case contributes its stated integral.
If the supporting intersection has zero section area, its contribution
is zero by the same dominated-convergence calculation.

The projection of the plane v.x=c onto v-perpendicular is an isometry,
so these are exactly H_(d-1) section measures, with no missing normal
factor. In particular normalization by |v|=1 is essential and is used
correctly. Summing the finitely many fibers gives

    g(e)=e.m+int min(0,e.(w-y)) dtheta_I
               +int max(0,e.(w-y)) dtheta_O.

This proves the source derivative formula without assuming smoothness,
strict convexity, a finite number of body facets, or a transverse cut.
Each original nonvertical cap plane has zero fiber d-volume. Closed
caps therefore cause no omitted d-volume term; their possibly positive
boundary section area is retained in theta_I and theta_O.

The perturbed continuous normal remains nonzero for all sufficiently
small t. Because each perturbed cap contains exactly y on its boundary,
depth attainment implies g(e)>=0 for every ambient e. A component of e
parallel to the old full normal has zero pairing on the cap plane, as
the source observes.

## 2. Zonoid inclusion and the direction of every sign

For each of the finite compactly supported section measures theta, the
densities 0<=alpha<=1 form a weak-* compact convex subset of L-infinity
(theta). Its finite vector-moment image is compact and convex. A
measurable density has a Borel representative modulo theta-null sets,
so this gives exactly the source's definition of Z(theta).

Its support function is

    h_Z(e)=int (e.(w-y))_+ dtheta.

Consequently

    int min(0,e.(w-y)) dtheta_I = -h_(-Z(theta_I))(e),

and

    g(e)=h_(m+Z(theta_O))(e)-h_(-Z(theta_I))(e).

The inequality for every e is therefore exactly

    -Z(theta_I) subset m+Z(theta_O).

For a prescribed inside moment z_I, this inclusion yields
-z_I=m+z_O for an outside moment z_O. Thus the vector identity is
m+z_I+z_O=0, with the signs and the quantifiers appearing in the source.
In particular it is **for every inside density, there exists an outside
density**, not merely the existence of one pair.

Adding g(e) and g(-e) cancels m and gives exactly

    int |e.(w-y)| dtheta_I <= int |e.(w-y)| dtheta_O.

This is an absolute-first-moment comparison. The source correctly does
not promote it to arbitrary convex order, a covariance inequality, or a
second-moment comparison.

## 3. The no-outside-facet consequence

If theta_O=0, the inclusion places -Z(theta_I) in the singleton {m}.
Since zero belongs to Z(theta_I), m=0 and Z(theta_I)={0}. Equivalently,
the absolute-first-moment comparison in every coordinate direction
implies w=y theta_I-almost everywhere.

An inside supporting facet cannot occur in the own fiber, because y is
an interior point there. All other fibers have a different base
coordinate. Thus none of these facets contains y, and theta_I=0.
The own proper section has strictly positive H_(d-1) measure, including
H_0 mass one when d=1. Hence theta_P has positive total mass and its
centroid is y because its centered first moment m is zero. No division
by a zero section mass occurs.

## 4. Prescribed allocations in the shape-stress argument

At each inside coincidence, for every prescribed Borel alpha in [0,1],

    min(r,ell)<=alpha r+(1-alpha)ell.

This is an upper bound for every feasible velocity, even if the fixed
alpha does not realize the actual min branch. Outside coincidences
continue to be represented exactly as the supremum of alpha(r+ell),
0<=alpha<=1. The proper-section and strictly-inside-body terms are
unchanged. Therefore the actual cap derivative is bounded above by the
supremum of the reduced gradient set after all inside allocations have
been prescribed. The robust separation proof uses only this upper
bound and remains valid.

On a finite parameter space, outside densities give a compact convex
moment set. The fixed inside densities only contribute fixed linear
forms. Common erosion r=-1 with ell=0 evaluates every gradient at a
strictly negative number: each selected cap has a positive-area own
body-boundary patch strictly inside it, while every other body
allocation is nonnegative. Fixing arbitrary inside allocations cannot
remove or reverse this patch's contribution. Thus the strict common
direction needed both for cone closedness and for the separating
improvement is retained.

The signed joint continuous homothety also retains its exact value.
It has r=n.x and ell=a.p-b=-v.x on the cap plane. On an inside
coincidence n=-v, so r=ell and every allocation gives the same value.
On an outside coincidence n=v, so r+ell=0 and every allocation gives
zero there. Equivalently, the exact homothety x->(1+t)x, accompanied by
a->(1+t)a and b->(1+t)b, multiplies every cap volume by (1+t)^d.
Thus every candidate gradient has value dQ, the total-volume objective
has value dM, and the same normalization sum(lambda)=1/beta follows.
No allocation-dependent normalization factor is introduced.

There is also no obstruction in the finite-intersection argument.
For fixed inside alpha and varying lambda, its weighted measure is
lambda alpha theta. The map lambda->lambda alpha theta is weakly
continuous even when alpha is merely Borel: for every continuous test f,
the moment is lambda times the fixed finite number int f alpha dtheta.
Thus the condition prescribing these weighted measures is closed in
the same compact certificate space. Outside measures retain their
usual domination and equality constraints. Every finite union of
body-test lists uses the same prescribed inside system and therefore
has a certificate. The finite-intersection property gives one
certificate for all such tests, for this system.

The resulting order of quantifiers is consequently

    for every admissible selected critical cover,
      for every prescribed inside-allocation system,
        there exists a normalized multiplier/outside-allocation
        certificate satisfying all the body-test constraints.

The certificate may change when the inside system changes. Nothing in
the argument exchanges these quantifiers. This is exactly the source's
claim, rather than a claim of a single certificate working for all
inside systems simultaneously.

## 5. Projective-orbit version and scope separation

For the fixed-body projective-orbit stress, the corresponding inside
term is min(0,ell)<=sigma ell for every prescribed sigma in [0,1].
Fixing these sigmas again leaves compact outside-allocation sets.
The common affine-density direction A=1 with fixed caps has value -dQ
on every cap gradient, independently of every section allocation, and
the total objective has value -dM. Hence strict separation and
sum(lambda)=1/beta are unaffected. The bulk signed-affine moment
certificate therefore has the same universal-inside quantifier.

This audits the conditional stationarity assertion only. It neither
asserts that a fixed-base shape minimum is a projective-orbit minimum,
nor identifies certificates from those distinct problems. The source
retains these distinctions. Unweighted projective transformations do
not preserve the lattice-complete OC class; none is being used here to
infer the false arbitrary-finite-base depth target.

## 6. Audit conclusion

All cap orientations allowed by the nonvertical hypothesis, all facet
coincidences, d=1 section atoms, arbitrary Borel inside allocations, and
the exact normalization have been checked. The proof omits neither
supporting facets nor boundary section measure. It is a valid necessary
condition for the stated positive-fiber extremal problems. It supplies
no missing numerical lattice/parity inequality and does not claim to
handle intrinsic lower-dimensional fibers or d=0 through these surface
variations.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
